questions.stem: Familial hypercholesterolemia results due to defects in which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
LDL receptor defect
  • Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a genetic disorder characterized by high cholesterol levels, specifically very high levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL cholesterol), in the blood and early cardiovascular diseases.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 31st Edition, Page No. 592

questions.stem: Metabolic lactic acidosis is seen in a patient due to a defect in the?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyruvate dehydrogenase
  • PDCD is generally presented in one of two forms. The metabolic form appears as lactic acidosis.
  • The neurological form of PDCD contributes to hypotonia, poor feeding, lethargy and structural abnormalities in the brain


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 309

questions.stemHtml: The following Lineweaver Burk plots depict enzymatic action in the presence of enzyme inhibitors. The enzyme action without inhibitors is represented by a black line. What type of inhibitors are A and B?

options.label: A
options.text: A- uncompetitive inhibition B- competitive inhibition

options.label: B
options.text: A- noncompetitive inhibition B- competitive inhibition

options.label: C
options.text: A- competitive inhibition B- uncompetitive inhibition

options.label: D
options.text: A- competitive inhibition B- noncompetitive inhibition

questions.answerText: A- noncompetitive inhibition B- competitive inhibition
questions.solutionHtml:
A- noncompetitive inhibition B- competitive inhibition
  • Enzyme inhibitors are molecules that interact with enzymes (temporary or permanent) in some way and reduce the rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction or prevent enzymes to work in a normal manner.
  • The important types of inhibitors are competitive, noncompetitive, and uncompetitive inhibitors


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 31st Edition, Page No. 322

questions.stem: All are true statements regarding folate deficiency except:

options.label: A
options.text: Increased levels of homocysteine and normal methylmalonic acid

options.label: B
options.text: Folate deficiency is commonly seen in children with hemolytic anemia

options.label: C
options.text: It is important to treat co-existing b12 deficiency before initiating folate therapy

options.label: D
options.text: Folate supplementation on diagnosis of pregnancy prevents neural tube defects

questions.answerText: Folate deficiency is commonly seen in children with hemolytic anemia
questions.solutionHtml:
Folate deficiency is commonly seen in children with hemolytic anemia
  • Folate is an essential water-soluble vitamin, naturally present in food, especially in fruits, green leafy vegetables, and liver.
  • Folic acid is the synthesized form of folate present in fortified foods and supplements and has a higher bioavailability than naturally occurring folate.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 1290

questions.stem: FISH technique helps to identify all except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Point mutation
  • It is now well established that denaturing or temperature gradient gel electrophoresis detects close to 100% of point mutations
  • Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is a molecular cytogenetic technique that allows the localization of a specific DNA sequence or an entire chromosome in a cell.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 1075

questions.stem: Which of the following micronutrients are associated with decreased sexual maturation and hypogonadism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zinc
  • Zn deficiency is correlated with reduction in testis volume, a decrease in testicular weight, hypogonadism, gonadal dysfunction, inadequate development of secondary sex specifications in human, shrinkage of seminiferous tubules, the failure of spermatogenesis, male gonad growth and hypogonadism


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 1321

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a heme breakdown product?
questions.solutionHtml:
ALA
  • δ-Aminolevulinic acid is an endogenous non-proteinogenic amino acid, is the first compound in the porphyrin synthesis pathway, the pathway that leads to heme in mammals.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 762

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a neurotransmitter derived from amino acids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Creatine
  • Creatine is found in vertebrates where it facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
  • Recycling is achieved by converting adenosine diphosphate (ADP) back to ATP via donation of phosphate groups.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 1369

questions.stem: Which of the following is not related to G6PD Deficiency?

options.label: B
options.text: Equal incidence in males and females

options.label: C
options.text: Predisposes the patient to oxidative stress

questions.answerText: Equal incidence in males and females
questions.solutionHtml:
Equal incidence in males and females
  • Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (G6PDD), also known as favism, is the most common enzyme deficiency anemia worldwide. Males are affected more often than females


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 31st Edition, Page No. 1586

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a post-transcriptional modification?
questions.solutionHtml:
Endonuclease cleavage
  • Endonucleases are enzymes that cleave the phosphodiester bond within a polynucleotide chain (namely DNA or RNA).
  • Some, such as deoxyribonuclease I, cut DNA relatively nonspecifically (without regard to sequence), while many, typically called restriction endonucleases or restriction enzymes, cleave only at very specific nucleotide sequences


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 31st Edition, Page No. 1694

questions.stem: Which type of mutation results in the reversal to wild type of phenotype when the mutant gene is suppressed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Reverse mutation
  • A mutation that alters the wild-type phenotype is called a forward mutation, whereas a reverse mutation (a reversion) changes a mutant phenotype back into the wild type.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 964

questions.stem: Which test will be done for detecting metabolite levels for inborn errors of metabolism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Next generation sequencing
  • Next-generation sequencing (NGS) is a technology for determining the sequence of DNA or RNA to study genetic variation associated with diseases or other biological phenomena.


Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 31st Edition, Page No. 1706
